contractPurpose: A minimal ETH wallet that accepts deposits from anyone and lets its owner sweep the entire balance to an address of their choice.
summary: Wallet stores the deploying account as owner (line 5), accepts plain ETH transfers (line 9) and exposes one function, sweep, that sends the whole balance to a caller-supplied address (lines 11-13). Access to sweep is decided with tx.origin instead of msg.sender (line 12). That combination lets a malicious contract the owner interacts with redirect the whole balance. There is no way to change the owner.
riskReasoning: The scanner's HIGH tx-origin signal is confirmed by the code: the only authorization check on a fund-moving function uses tx.origin. The fund-withdrawal signal is also confirmed: sweep moves the full balance in one call. Together these are the basis for HIGH. The code is short and fully visible, so no unseen inheritance is assumed.

keyFunctions.name: sweep
keyFunctions.description: Sends the contract's entire ETH balance to the address passed as `to`, if tx.origin equals owner.

keyFunctions.name: receive
keyFunctions.description: Accepts plain ETH transfers with no logic.

permissions.role: owner (set to the deployer at line 5)
capabilities: sweep the full ETH balance to any address

externalCalls.description: Sends ETH with the fixed 2300 gas stipend of transfer (line 13).

securityFindings.title: Authorization based on tx.origin
securityFindings.observed: Line 12 requires tx.origin == owner before sweep sends the whole balance (line 13).
securityFindings.potentialRisk: If the owner ever calls a malicious contract, that contract could call sweep in the same transaction; tx.origin would still be the owner, so the check passes and the funds could go to an address the attacker picks.

securityFindings.title: Entire balance movable by a single account in one call
securityFindings.observed: sweep (line 11) is external and transfers address(this).balance (line 13) to any address given by the caller.
securityFindings.potentialRisk: Safety depends entirely on protection of the owner key; there is no limit, delay or second approver.

securityFindings.title: Owner cannot be changed
securityFindings.observed: owner is assigned once at line 5 and no function in the provided source modifies it.
securityFindings.potentialRisk: If the owner key is lost, the balance cannot be withdrawn; if it is compromised, the owner cannot be rotated.

interactionRisks.description: A phishing or malicious contract that the owner interacts with could trigger sweep on the owner's behalf.
interactionRisks.dependsOn: the owner calling an attacker-controlled contract

interactionRisks.description: Sweeping to a contract address whose receive/fallback needs more than 2300 gas would revert.
interactionRisks.dependsOn: `to` being a contract with a non-trivial fallback

recommendations: Confirm whether authorization should use msg.sender instead of tx.origin.
Check how the owner key is stored and whether a multisig or ownership-transfer mechanism is expected.
Check whether sweeping to contract recipients (2300 gas limit of transfer) is a supported use case.
limitations: Only the provided source text was analyzed; the contract was not compiled, deployed or executed.
The source is a single file with no imports or inheritance.
